content:
Alice: Quick summary of the GPTQ bakeoff across Llama / Mistral / Qwen — ran GPTQ, AWQ, INT8 and FP8 across representative 7B and 13B configs. Posting aggregated deltas vs fp16 baseline and short deployment notes.

Ben: awesome, curious about MMLU and conv benchmarks.

Alice: top-line numbers first (mean delta in percentage points vs fp16 baseline, lower is worse):
- Llama-2-13B (GPTQ 4-bit): MMLU -0.6, TruthfulQA -0.9, Perplexity +1.8
- Llama-2-13B (AWQ 4-bit): MMLU -0.8, TruthfulQA -1.1, Perplexity +2.2
- Mistral-7B (GPTQ 4-bit): MMLU -0.4, TruthfulQA -0.6, Perplexity +1.5
- Qwen-7B (GPTQ 4-bit): MMLU -0.9, TruthfulQA -1.3, Perplexity +2.7
- Mistral-7B (FP8 experimental): MMLU +0.0, TruthfulQA -0.2, Perplexity +0.5
- INT8 dynamic (all fams): larger PPL hit on long contexts, avg MMLU -1.5

Carol: so FP8 wins for Mistral-7B on quality, but what's the throughput / memory tradeoff?

Alice: yes — FP8 gave near-zero quality delta for Mistral at 7B but required custom kernels and ~1.2x memory compared to GPTQ 4-bit (because FP8 runtime currently keeps some tensors in FP16 for stability). GPTQ 4-bit gives ~2.8x memory reduction vs fp16 and 1.9x throughput improvement on our T4/RTX benchmarks. AWQ slightly slower than GPTQ for decode due to per-group scaling steps.

DevBot: CI run finished for batch job 6723 — all quantized model artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/gptq-bakeoff/1720754321/

Alice: reproducible command we used for GPTQ (example):
```bash
python run_quant.py \
  --model-dir s3://models/llama2-13b/fp16 \
  --out-dir /tmp/quant/llama2-13b-gptq-4bit \
  --method gptq \
  --bits 4 \
  --group-size 128 \
  --calib-samples 2048 \
  --eval-sets mmlu,truthfulqa,pile-perplexity
```

Eva: thanks — did you calibrate with chat-style prompts for Qwen? it's sensitive to prompt structure.

Alice: good call. For Qwen we included 50% chat-like calibration windows and 50% long-form docs. That reduced hallucination regression vs a docs-only calibration set.

Frank: any failure modes to watch for in production?

Alice: two things:
1) KV cache mismatch for some GPTQ kernels — we saw 0.5% token-drop errors on very long multi-turn convs; workaround was a small patch to cache alignment (we added a micro-fix in runtime v1.12).
2) Serving cold-start perf — quantized models need a slightly longer warm-up (extra 10–20ms per worker) if using on-demand JITed kernels. We add a warmup job in Dedicated pools.

Ben: deployment profiles? which configs are ready for Dedicated vs Private?

Alice: recommendation:
- Dedicated: GPTQ 4-bit for Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B (best cost/quality). Use streamed prefix caching and batching.
- Private (on-prem): FP8 for Mistral-7B if you can accept custom kernel install and slightly higher memory — best quality for regulated customers.
- Hosted API: stick with FP16 or INT8 dynamic for Qwen-7B family until we stabilize GPTQ kernels for chat-style workloads.

Carol: can we add small automated evals in the rollout pipeline so we catch regressions?

Alice: already added an eval gate: when a quantized artifact is produced we run a 10k-query lightweight suite (subset of MMLU + safety + 1k conv QA). If MMLU delta > 1.0 pp or safety regressions flagged, artifact fails rollout.

DevBot: rollout gate configured (project: quant-bakeoff) — notifications to #eng-ml and #eng-releases.

Eva: can you drop the S3 paths for artifacts and the evaluation CSVs?

Alice: s3://redwood-evals/gptq-bakeoff/1720754321/artifacts/
s3://redwood-evals/gptq-bakeoff/1720754321/evals/summary.csv — contains per-model per-method deltas and raw scores.

Frank: thanks — I'll sync with infra to schedule Dedicated pool tests next week. :thumbsup:

Alice: cool, will follow up with a short doc and a slide for next eng sync. If anyone wants raw logs or the eval harness config ping me.

Ben: great work, Alice. :clap:
